raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Outside the replicated layout, each worker only uses its own slot of every row in the shared CPU region, yet every worker `cudaHostRegister`s the whole region. At TP4, every page gets pinned four times.

Register only the worker's slot of each row, rounded out to pages. The replicated layout keeps whole-region registration. So do slots within a page of the full row and regions over 65,536 rows, where per-call overhead would dominate.

TieringOffloadingSpec workers pin through the same path, so they get this too. #59430 lists this redundant pinning as a follow-up, and no open PR changes it.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 34.8 s, and pinning from 20.8 to 6.8 s, as each rank registered 68.8 GB instead of 274.9 GB. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

nodes.body: An independent data point supporting this: when several processes pin the same region, as the TP ranks do on main, the pin time grows with TP. For 100 GB it went from about 9 s with one process to 31 s with eight. I also tried threading the registration within one process instead. It gave no speedup. So pinning less, as this PR does, looks like the right fix. Details are [here](https://github.com/YannikHinteregger/vllm-cpu-pin-benchmarks).

nodes.body:
How did you determine 65,536?

Above that many rows we fall back to pinning the whole region. More offload memory means more rows, so the big setups that would gain the most from this change don't get it. E.g. Llama-3-70B at TP4 has 5 MiB rows, so anything above 320 GiB already falls back.

I think the number of rows doesn't matter much here. Every call costs a bit but also saves the other ranks part of that row. So with twice the rows we pay twice as much but also save twice as much. 

I think row size should be how we decide wether we turn this off.
A log line when we fall back would also be nice.

inline_comments.body:
How did you determine 65,536?

Above that many rows we fall back to pinning the whole region. More offload memory means more rows, so the big setups that would gain the most from this change don't get it. E.g. Llama-3-70B at TP4 has 5 MiB rows, so anything above 320 GiB already falls back.

I think the number of rows doesn't matter much here. Every call costs a bit but also saves the other ranks part of that row. So with twice the rows we pay twice as much but also save twice as much. 

I think row size should be how we decide wether we turn this off.
A log line when we fall back would also be nice.

issue_comments.body: An independent data point supporting this: when several processes pin the same region, as the TP ranks do on main, the pin time grows with TP. For 100 GB it went from about 9 s with one process to 31 s with eight. I also tried threading the registration within one process instead. It gave no speedup. So pinning less, as this PR does, looks like the right fix. Details are [here](https://github.com/YannikHinteregger/vllm-cpu-pin-benchmarks).
